newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Coalition deal not sum of NZ govt's agenda - Bolger.
newsitem.headline: Coalition deal not sum of NZ govt's agenda - Bolger.

text.p: Prime Minister Jim Bolger on Tuesday told a business audience that while the Coalition Agreement would form the core of the government's agenda in the next three years, it was not the sum.
"But let me be clear, it is not, and neither does it claim to be, the sum total of our likely programme."
He said it just set out the fiscal and strategic priorities and the principles that underlie them.
Sometimes there would be disagreements, he said.
Bolger said his government would maintain fiscal restraint.
"As a prime minister I believe that I have a track record for ensuring fiscal restraint and sound economic policies.
"Let me assure you that I have no intention of compromising that reputation now," he said.
Those departmental chiefs should put their pet spending projects back on the shelf, he said.
"Some may even find themselves wishing for the 'good old days' of having to deal just with (Finance Minister Bill) Mr Birch," Bolger said.
The government would last the distance because it had agreed on aspirations and priciples that would keep it on track, he said.
